subject: Clarify: MSA PO-acceptance redline + Ariba identity/EDI handshake
messages:
From: Lynn Carter <lynn.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procure-support@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor onboarding questions + MSA redline (PO acceptance)

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement ran our MSA redline by Legal and they've pushed back on the PO acceptance language in Section 4.2 (it currently states explicit "acknowledgement" timing that conflicts with our Ariba automation). Attached is the redline they returned (Acme_MSA_redline_v3.docx).

Two asks to help unblock onboarding:
- Can Redwood accept our alternate PO-acceptance clause that leaves automated acknowledgement responsibility with Acme's Ariba routing?
- Does Redwood require an identity-broker (SAML/Okta) for vendor registration into Acme's Ariba, or can we use certificate-based SFTP + partner token?

Procurement would like the vendor onboarding to hit: staging portal registration -> EDI 850 PO acceptance -> PO ACK in 24 hours. If Redwood needs changes to our EDI field map we can provide a sample 850 file.

I looped in procure-support for files. Please advise next steps and who we should expect from Redwood Legal/Integrations.

Thanks,
Lynn Carter
Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Health
attachments: Acme_MSA_redline_v3.docx

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Lynn Carter <lynn.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding questions + MSA redline (PO acceptance)

Lynn — thanks for sharing and for the clear asks. We can definitely move this forward. High-level:

- Legal (Kimberly) will review the redline and propose compromise language for Section 4.2 that preserves Redwood's obligation to acknowledge POs without changing your Ariba automation semantics.
- Integrations (Marcus) will validate whether an identity broker is required for Acme's enrollment pattern, or whether certificate + partner token is sufficient for EDI/Ariba.
- We'll need a sample 850 (or the EDI schema columns) to confirm PO field mapping and whether any PO-ACK timing constraints require a workflow change on our side.

Next steps we propose:
1) Kimberly to review and provide markups (legal) by EOD Monday 7/20.
2) Marcus to validate identity/transport requirements and return suggested integration approach + gaps by Tue 7/21.
3) Lynn/procure-support to send a sample 850 (or CSV mapping) — that will let Marcus produce a quick EDI_field_map_v1.csv.

Kimberly/Marcus — can you confirm timelines above? Lynn, I added the HubSpot deal ID to the thread for traceability.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Lynn Carter <lynn.carter@acmehealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding questions + MSA redline (PO acceptance)

Priyom/Lynn — I reviewed the attached redline. Notes below (high level):

- Section 4.2 (PO acceptance): Acme's proposed language removes Redwood's obligation to timely acknowledge certain POs. We can't accept language that creates an open-ended acceptance window — that materially increases financial/fulfillment risk.
- Compromise: We can accept language that allows Acme's Ariba automation to drive "order creation" semantics provided Redwood retains the obligation to send a PO-acknowledgement (simple ACK) within 24 business hours of receipt for non-automated exceptions. I've drafted a proposed paragraph and attached it as Redwood_PO_acceptance_compromise.docx.
- Audit/logging: Redwood can provide request/response traces and audit logs for up to 1 year (SOC 2 evidence available). If Acme requires longer retention, that's an add-on; please specify.

Requested edits from Acme Legal to accept compromise: replace Section 4.2 redline with the attached paragraph and confirm that automated Ariba routing won't be interpreted as acceptance when exceptions are flagged.

Attachments: Redwood_PO_acceptance_compromise.docx

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lynn Carter <lynn.carter@acmehealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding questions + MSA redline (PO acceptance)

Lynn — quick tech summary based on initial portal spec: 

- Identity: For standard Acme Ariba supplier flows we support both: (A) identity broker (SAML/Okta) for portal SSO, and (B) certificate-based SFTP + partner token for machine-to-machine EDI. If you want a single-signup path from Ariba to Redwood Console we'd recommend the SAML broker — otherwise the certificate + token route is lower-friction for automated EDI only.
- EDI/PO ACK: Redwood consumes 850/POs and emits a standard 855 ACK. We are able to send the 855 within your 24-hour window for non-exception POs. Exceptions (e.g., price mismatch) will generate an exception workflow; those won't be auto-accepted.
- Mapping: attached is a first-pass EDI_field_map_v1.csv that maps Acme's PO fields to Redwood's internal order schema. Two fields to flag: PO_LINE_ITEM_UOM (unit of measure) and PO_CUSTOM_REF — both currently require a small transform on our side; we can handle it but would like a sample 850.

Please send a sample 850 (or CSV export) to integrations@redwood.com; I'll validate end-to-end in staging. I've also attached sample_850_edi.xml for reference.

Marcus Lin
Engineering Lead, Integrations | Redwood Inference
attachments: EDI_field_map_v1.csv, sample_850_edi.xml

From: Lynn Carter <lynn.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procure-support@acmehealth.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding questions + MSA redline (PO acceptance)

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turn.

Acme Legal reviewed Kimberly's compromise paragraph and are agreeable to the wording in Redwood_PO_acceptance_compromise.docx, provided we get the logging/audit detail called out in a short SLA annex. I'll have Legal prepare that annex and upload through DocuSign.

Procurement will also push a sanitized sample 850 by EOD tomorrow to integrations@redwood.com. We are prepared to proceed with certificate-based SFTP + partner token for initial production; we'll revisit SAML broker for future single-signup.

Next steps (agreed):
- Acme Legal to upload annex via DocuSign (linked: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/abc123-redwood-acme).
- Acme to send sample 850 to Marcus.
- Priyom to share updated order form once annex is attached.

I'll mark HubSpot CR-8542 as "contract redline agreed — awaiting annex" and loop in our procurement ops team if any delays.

Best,
Lynn
Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Health
